title: Rules of the Road (Core)
content:
Core Principles

Safe driving depends on planning ahead, staying within speed limits, and obeying road signs and signals. Always drive at a speed that allows you to stop safely within the distance you can see to be clear.

Speed Limits (Cars)

  • Built-up areas: 30 mph unless signs show otherwise
  • Single carriageways: 60 mph
  • Dual carriageways: 70 mph
  • Motorways: 70 mph

Important: Speed limits can be lower where signs indicate, especially near schools, road works, or in residential zones.

Stopping Distances

Stopping distance = Thinking distance + Braking distance.

  • 30 mph: 23m
  • 40 mph: 36m
  • 50 mph: 53m
  • 60 mph: 73m
  • 70 mph: 96m

Following Distance

Use the 2-second rule in dry conditions and at least 4 seconds in wet conditions.

References

See the official Highway Code for authoritative rules and updates: gov.uk/guidance/the-highway-code

title: Traffic Signs
content:
Sign Categories

  • Warning signs (red triangle): hazards ahead
  • Regulatory signs (circle): mandatory or prohibitive instructions
  • Information signs (rectangle): directions, services, and routes

Common Examples

  • Stop (red octagon): must stop and give way
  • Give Way (red triangle): slow and yield if needed
  • No entry (red circle): do not enter
  • Mandatory direction (blue circle): you must follow

References

Official guidance: Highway Code – Traffic signs

title: Road Markings
content:
Center Lines

  • Broken white line: you may cross if safe
  • Double white lines, broken on your side: you may cross if safe and necessary
  • Double white lines, solid on your side: do not cross unless safe and necessary to pass a stationary vehicle or overtake a cyclist/horse at very low speed

Stop Lines

Stop behind the solid line at traffic lights or STOP signs.

Box Junctions

Do not enter unless your exit is clear. You may turn right if waiting for oncoming traffic and your exit is clear.

References

Highway Code: Road markings

title: Traffic Lights and Signals
content:
Traffic Lights

  • Red: Stop
  • Red + Amber: Prepare to go (do not move until green)
  • Green: Proceed if clear
  • Amber: Stop unless unsafe to do so

Filter Arrows

A green arrow means you may proceed in the arrow direction only if safe.

Flashing Amber

At pedestrian crossings, you may proceed if the crossing is clear.

References

Highway Code signals: Traffic light signals

title: Junctions and Roundabouts
content:
Junctions

Approach with caution, check mirrors, signal early, and position correctly. Give way to traffic on the main road.

Roundabouts

Give way to traffic approaching from your right. Signal left to exit. Use the correct lane and stay aware of lane markings and signs.

Mini-roundabouts

You must pass around the central markings (do not drive over unless it's unavoidable due to vehicle size).

References

Highway Code: Using the road

title: Motorways and Dual Carriageways
content:
Joining Motorways

Use the slip road to build speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge safely.

Lane Discipline

Keep left unless overtaking. Move back to the left when safe.

Smart Motorways

Follow overhead gantry signs. If a lane is marked with a red X, it is closed.

Hard Shoulder

Only use in emergencies unless signs show it is open as a running lane.

References

Motorway rules: Motorways (rules 253–273)

title: Vulnerable Road Users
content:
Pedestrians

Give extra time and space to children, older people, and those with disabilities. Be prepared to stop at crossings.

Cyclists

Leave at least 1.5 meters when overtaking. Check for cyclists before opening doors.

Motorcyclists

They may be hard to see. Check blind spots carefully before changing lanes.

Horse Riders

Pass slowly and give at least a car’s width when safe.

References

Hierarchy of road users: Highway Code Introduction

title: Vehicle Safety and Maintenance
content:
Pre-drive Checks

  • Tyres: minimum tread depth 1.6mm
  • Lights: all working
  • Windscreen: clear and undamaged
  • Fluids: oil, coolant, brake fluid, washer
  • Mirrors: adjusted

MOT

Vehicles over 3 years old require an annual MOT certificate.

Warning Lights

  • Red: stop safely, serious issue
  • Amber: check soon
  • Green/Blue: information only

References

MOT guidance: gov.uk/getting-an-mot

title: Driving in Different Conditions
content:
Wet Weather

Reduce speed, increase following distance (at least 4 seconds), and avoid harsh braking.

Fog

Use fog lights when visibility is less than 100 meters. Turn them off when visibility improves.

Night Driving

Use dipped headlights in built-up areas and when following other vehicles. Use full beam on unlit roads when safe.

Snow and Ice

Drive slowly, use higher gears, brake gently, and increase following distance up to 10 times normal.

References

Bad weather advice: Highway Code – Adverse weather

title: Hazard Awareness and Defensive Driving
content:
Hazard Perception

Scan far ahead, check mirrors every 5–8 seconds, and anticipate other road users’ actions.

Defensive Driving

Always assume others may make mistakes. Keep safe distances and plan escape routes.

Common Hazards

  • Pedestrians near crossings
  • Cyclists and motorcyclists in blind spots
  • Road works and temporary signs
  • Weather changes

References

Hazard awareness guidance: Highway Code – Using the road

title: Safety, Seatbelts, and Passengers
content:
Seatbelts

Drivers and passengers must wear seatbelts unless exempt. The driver is responsible for ensuring children are properly restrained.

Child Seats

Children must use the correct car seat for their height and weight as per UK law.

Distractions

Do not use a handheld mobile phone while driving. Avoid distractions that reduce your focus.

References

Seatbelt law: gov.uk/seat-belts-law

title: Alcohol, Drugs, and Fitness to Drive
content:
Alcohol

Never drive if you feel impaired. The safest limit is zero. Alcohol affects judgement, reaction time, and coordination.

Drugs

Driving under the influence of illegal or prescription drugs can be dangerous and illegal. Always check medication labels.

Fatigue

If you feel sleepy, stop safely, take a break, and rest.

References

Drink-driving rules: gov.uk/drink-drive-limit

title: Documents, Insurance, and Enforcement
content:
Documents

  • Driving licence
  • Vehicle tax (Vehicle Excise Duty)
  • Valid insurance
  • MOT (if required)

Insurance

You must have at least third-party insurance to drive a car on UK roads.

Penalties

Breaking driving laws can result in fines, penalty points, or disqualification.

References

Driving documents: gov.uk driving licences

title: Breakdowns and Incidents
content:
Breakdown Safety

If safe, pull over, switch on hazard lights, and move behind a barrier. Call for assistance.

Warning Triangle

Use on roads (not motorways) to warn other drivers. Place it at least 45m behind your vehicle.

Incidents

Stop if involved in a collision. Exchange details and report to police when required.

References

Breakdown advice: Highway Code – Breakdowns

title: Eco-Driving and Vehicle Loading
content:
Eco-Driving

Drive smoothly, anticipate traffic, and avoid harsh acceleration. Maintain correct tyre pressures and remove unnecessary weight from the car.

Vehicle Loading

Load should be secure and not obstruct your view. Heavy items should be placed low and as far forward as possible.

References

Eco-driving tips: gov.uk/eco-driving
